ra: Jah is the supreme God of the Rastafari movement.
Haile Selassie I is the central venerated figure of the Rastafari movement.
Marcus Garvey is received within Rastafari as a prophet-forerunner of the movement.
Babylon is a core theological concept of the Rastafari movement.
Zion is a core theological concept of the Rastafari movement.
Jah derives from Jehovah, a vocalization of the Tetragrammaton YHWH (Yahweh), received via the King James Bible (Psalm 68:4).
The Rastafari concept of Babylon draws on the biblical Babylon / Whore of Babylon of Revelation as the symbol of corrupt worldly power.
In Rastafari theology Babylon (the oppressive system) stands in opposition to Zion (the promised land).
Many Rastafari adherents venerate Haile Selassie I as the returned Christ; this models that belief held within the tradition as a reception of the figure of Jesus Christ.
Haile Selassie's imperial legitimacy is grounded in the Ethiopian Solomonic dynasty traced to Menelik I, central to Rastafari's Ethiopianist theology.
In the Kebra Nagast tradition Menelik I is the son of Makeda, Queen of Sheba; cited within Rastafari to ground the Solomonic line venerated in the movement.
